messages:
Tara (CS): Customer reports inconsistent outputs after yesterday's routing rollout. Same exact prompt sometimes returns old behavior and sometimes the new one. Example: request_id=req_0ab12 — prompt: "What is the capital of Freedonia?" sometimes -> "Sylvania", sometimes -> "Eastport". They call this a regression and are upset.

Maya (Support): Ack — sorry about that. Can you paste the full request payload + the X-Request-Id header and the customer_id? Also any example timestamps helps.

Tara (CS): Paste below (redacted customer id).
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX
X-Request-Id: req_0ab12
{
  "model": "redwood-v2",
  "input": "What is the capital of Freedonia?",
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 32
}
```
Happened 2025-11-04T18:12:03Z and again at 2025-11-04T18:12:17Z (different outputs). Customer ID: cust_945.

Joel (SRE): Looking at routing logs for cust_945 around those times. Snippet: 
```
2025-11-04T18:12:03Z route_decision=primary_pool target=redwood-v2-pt request_id=req_0ab12
2025-11-04T18:12:17Z route_decision=fallback target=redwood-v2-quant request_id=req_0ab12 reason=primary_capacity_spike
```
So the same customer request_id was routed to two different model variants (pt vs quant) due to a transient capacity condition.

Liam (ML Eng): That explains variant mismatch. Important: quantized variant has a slightly different tokenizer/rounding and we also ship a different sampling default for low-temp deterministic paths (small implementation diff) which can change facts at temp=0.0. Even with temp=0, subtle differences in tokenization + logits rounding can flip the first token.

Maya (Support): Temporary mitigations for customer: 1) Ask them to pin the model variant in the request (they can use the model_version or variant_override param). Example: 
```json
{"model": "redwood-v2", "variant_override": "pt", "input": "What is the capital of Freedonia?", "temperature": 0.0}
```
2) Or set a request header: `X-Redwood-Variant: pt`. This forces consistent variant until policy changes.

Liam (ML Eng): Long-term fix: we should enforce parity on deterministic inference paths across variants or restrict fallbacks for requests that set temperature=0.0. Also add a routing-safety check: if two variants produce different deterministic first-token at temp=0, prefer the canonical variant.

Joel (SRE): For immediate action I created a route patch to stop falling back to quant variants for customers with active SLOs on output-determinism. Patch id: route_patch_531. Will roll out canary and monitor.

DeployBot: canary_rollout route_patch_531 -> 3 hosts -> success (2025-11-04T18:45:00Z) :white_check_mark:

Maya (Support): Noted. I've sent the workaround steps to the customer (pin to pt) and escalated for a dedicated capacity offer. They replied they're OK to pin for now but want assurance this won't recur.

Joel (SRE): Follow-up: adding telemetry flag `deterministic_request=true` when temp<=0.01 so fallback decisions consider determinism going forward. I'll open RFC and timeline.

Tara (CS): Customer accepted the pin workaround for the short term. They asked for a changelog entry and rollback ETA. They're happy to wait for the canary results. :thumbsup:

Liam (ML Eng): I'll prioritize a parity test across variants and run a small eval on our regression suite for common QA prompts.

Maya (Support): Closing loop: ticket created INC-2025-7893, workaround documented, SRE/ML assigned. Will update the customer once rollback or hotfix is in prod.

Tara (CS): Thanks all, will follow up with customer later today.
